newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 5.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said he was open to government proposals to bring forward the 1998 budget as long as it contained structural measures to cut social welfare spending. Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said this was "a move to sink the government" (all).

* German chancellor Helmut Kohl said both Italy and Germany should "do their homeworks" to prepare for EMU in what was seen as a relaxing step after German businessmen said during the weekend they doubted Italy would make it in the first wave. Kohl is due to meet Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Friday 7 (all).
* Seventy deputies are expected to nominate today PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema chairman of a bi-cameral commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms (all).

* Metalworkers unions and employers signed a deal on contracts ending a long-running pay dispute. The government-brokered deal is based on a 30-month contract and a one-off payment of 512,000 lire paid in two instalments to cover the first six months, followed by a graduated monthly wage increase totalling 200,000 lire during the rest of the contract (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the sale of yellow pages publishing group SEAT will be completed by next spring. SEAT was floated off from state-controlled telecoms group Stet at the beginning of this year with state industrial group IRI holding a 61 percent stake. The privatisation of motorway operator Autostrade could be finalised by the start of the summer. Ciampi added the government wants a golden share in the privatisation of Stet and intends to create a hard core of masinly Italian shareholders who do not have related activities to telecommunications (all).
* Agro-industry and chemicals group Montedison reported 1996 net operating profits of 1.995 trillion lire after 1.912 trillion in 1995 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
